final.title: Attribution starts with one source field you can trust
final.body:
If you care about attribution, the first question is not which dashboard to buy. It is whether every lead already passes through one place where source can be recorded reliably. If it does not, attribution is a data-plumbing problem before it is an AI problem.

For a small business owner, the practical check is simple: look at the workflow that creates the lead — website form, email reply, CRM entry, or sales record — and ask whether source is being captured in the same way every time. If the answer depends on memory, a spreadsheet note, or whatever someone typed last Tuesday, the measurement is already shaky.

The next step is a small manual spot-check. Pick a recent handful of closed deals, trace each one back to the original trail, and compare that with the source field in your CRM or tracking sheet. A small sample will not prove the whole system is sound, but it will show whether the control is real or just decorative. Decorative controls are very efficient right up until you need them.

If the source field is blank, inconsistent, or routinely overwritten, fix the input rule before adding AI. Once the source data is reliable, then you can decide whether lead scoring, channel-based replies, or another automation is worth testing. Before that, the model would only help you measure noise more neatly.
